audiospeed_oracle: CircuitPython 10.2.1 source plus MicroPython executable regression
cpython_stdout_sha256_by_arch_note: Empty since 2026-09-17, and that is the result rather than the absence of one. aarch64 held the only entry this file has ever carried: six blocks of multitap and pitchshift one byte from x86_64, accepted 2026-09-02 and re-accepted 2026-09-03 under the byte-checksum probe format. audiodsp#79 gave every src/shared/ file that computes in float the shared/audiodsp_fp_contract.h pragma, aarch64 stopped fusing, and the six blocks closed -- so the allowance was removed rather than re-recorded, and aarch64 is held to cpython_stdout_sha256 like the reference architecture is. See cpython_stdout_sha256_reproduced_by. An architecture that genuinely differs still earns an entry here: the hash, the date, and the evidence a human judged on, per the 2026-09-02 rule that bit-identity is required within one architecture and not across.

aarch64.evidence: Reproduces cpython_stdout_sha256 (ff57b9ea0989dbbfe2357cd05f38beb83bf6468839aa7969ad7c37cf52644ebc), re-captured for audiodsp#201 when the oracle moved to CircuitPython 11.0.0-alpha.1, exactly: the four ubuntu-24.04-arm cells (Python 3.11 to 3.14) of CI run 37877744831 on PR #215 pass verify_effects.py, which holds aarch64 to this hash with no allowance. Before that, from 2026-09-17, it reproduced the previous hash (544d29ca31973613163977b2f1ef7b6e2ab04bc4881cc25f3df3acafcdfd95a3) the same way, in CI runs 35269077774 and 35269087728 on PR #86: the old divergence was compiler contraction and nothing else, closed by audiodsp#79's fp-contract header.
